contexts.text: The Lord does not break fallacies or extinguish cupidities, but bends to what is good and true. AC 1255. AC 1874. AC 1992:4. AC 2053:2. AC 2180:5. AC 6472:2.
As soon as a man's loves are broken...
Under Beginning, see this reference.
Under Bread, see these references. AC 3863:14. AC 9412:6. TCR 433:end. SE 2626. AE 295:11. AE 675:12.
The arms of war are broken () when, on the cessation of cupidities and falsities, a man comes into the tranquillity of peace.
Broken feet and hands () represented those who are in perverted outward worship.
The chief reason for this vastation and desolation is that the persuasive may be broken...
Unless the affection be broken...
The city of emptiness which is broken () = that the human mind is deprived of truth.
Not to break a bone (), in the supreme sense = not to do violence to Divine truth, and in the representative sense = not to do violence to the truth of any good.

Provision is here expressed in the Original Language by a word which means breaking, because in the Ancient Church bread was broken when it was given to another, and by this was signified to communicate from one's own, and to appropriate what is good from one's own, and so effect mutual love; for when bread is broken and given to another, it is then communicated from one's own; or when bread is broken among many, one bread becomes mutual, consequently there is conjunction through charity.
The Angels are forbidden to act violently, and thus break a man's cupidities and principles...
Under Bone, see this reference.
This (hereditary evil) can only be broken and altered through a life of faith and charity... TCR 521:3.
The Lord never breaks such truth with man, but so far as possible bends it. Example(s).
If it die or be bruised () = loss or injury. Breach and being broken, in the Word = dissipation, and also injury. Explained, Illustrated. AC 9175. AE 304:26.
Breach in these passages = injury done to the truths and goods of faith.
Under Bow, see this reference.
The breach of the people () = falsity of doctrine gradually creeping in from the wickedness of the teachers, from concupiscences, and other causes. AE 962:5.
To be broken () = to dissipate truths and goods.

He cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mountain () = the outward sense of the Word changed and different on account of that nation... To cast them out of his hands and break = to destroy the genuine outward sense.
Ye shall break their statues () = that the falsities of evil are to be dissipated.
That they so immersed themselves in falsities that nothing of truth remained, is described by the breaking of the potter's bottles ().
Under Heart, see these references. AE 811:18.
The great horn broken () = divided into many falsities which were born therefrom.
Broken pits which do not hold waters () = to hatch doctrinal things from their Own intelligence, which, being from proprium, are false.
Occurs. AE 817:9.
